paper_title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
core_problem: Existing LLM-based multi-agent systems can solve simple dialogue tasks but suffer logic inconsistencies and cascading hallucinations when naively chaining LLMs for more complex tasks, limiting reliable automated problem solving.
methodology_summary: MetaGPT is a meta-programming framework that encodes Standardized Operating Procedures into prompt sequences for streamlined workflows, allowing agents with human-like domain expertise to verify intermediate results and reduce errors. It uses an assembly line paradigm to assign diverse roles to agents and efficiently break down complex tasks into subtasks performed collaboratively.
empirical_results: On code generation benchmarks, MetaGPT achieves state-of-the-art Pass@1 of 85.9% on HumanEval and 87.7% on MBPP. On collaborative software engineering benchmarks it generates more coherent solutions than previous chat-based multi-agent systems, outperforming frameworks such as AutoGPT for complex software project creation.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly stated in provided context.
